quizzes.stem: A bank's loan flow must always check identity, then credit, then ask a person to approve, and an interrupted application must not repeat the credit check. Which style fits?

options.a: A single prompt, because the order is stated in the text of the call
options.b: A model-driven loop, because the model picks each next step on its own
options.c: A typed agent, because the loan is a record of fixed shape and size
options.d: A graph, because each node saves state and resumes after a stop

explanation.d: The page says "Checkpointers persist a thread's graph state as checkpoints", and a resumed run "repeats no earlier node", so the credit check is not paid for twice.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the table gives the next step to "The model, at each turn", and the loan order must always be fixed.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a typed agent has "Validated output" but "Types guard the edges of the model's freedom. They do not choose the route."
explanation.a: Ruled out because a prompt keeps no state, and the page gives the graph, not the prompt, the job of resuming: "the run resumes from the last checkpoint".

quizzes.stem: A team's agent receives a request type nobody planned for. Which style handles it with the least extra code?

options.a: A model-driven loop, since the model chooses its own steps
options.b: A graph with a node written for every request type that may arrive
options.c: A graph, since a missing edge falls back to the last node of the flow
options.d: A fixed script, since the replies follow a template that was written

explanation.a: The page says the model-driven route is "whatever the model chooses, so the same code handles a case nobody planned for."
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a case you did not draw has no path", and there is no fallback edge.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the graph is for a process that is "known and must be auditable", and a node for every type is the elaborate logic the model-driven authors reject: "elaborate orchestration logic, state machines, and predefined workflows".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a script is a route drawn in advance, and "a case you did not draw has no path".

quizzes.stem: A model-driven loop calls a tool again and again and never produces a final reply. What does the engineering post recommend?

options.a: A second model that repeats the same call for confirmation
options.b: A larger context window, so that the loop can finish its work
options.c: A stopping condition such as a maximum number of iterations
options.d: A typed schema, which ends the loop when the data is valid

explanation.c: The post lists "stopping conditions (such as a maximum number of iterations) to maintain control."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a loop that never ends must be cut off", and a larger window does not give the loop an end.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a repeat of the same call adds cost without a stop, and "Agentic systems often trade latency and cost for better task performance".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a schema checks shape, and "Validation proves the shape", not that a loop has finished.

quizzes.stem: A team's feature is one model call that summarises a document, with retrieved passages added to the prompt. What does the engineering advice suggest?

options.a: A graph framework that saves the single call as a checkpoint file
options.b: Improving the lone request with in-context examples and a search step
options.c: A managed agent that runs outside the service, with no code inside it
options.d: A multi-agent system in which one agent reviews another agent's work

explanation.b: The post says "For many applications, however, optimizing single LLM calls with retrieval and in-context examples is usually enough."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says a framework "earns its place when the feature it brings is one you need", and one call needs no checkpoint.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the advice is "finding the simplest solution possible, and only increasing complexity when needed."
explanation.c: Ruled out because Managed Agents is chosen when "The task is long-running or asynchronous", and this is one short call.

quizzes.stem: A developer reports that a framework agent gives odd answers and that nobody can see the text sent to the model. Which cost of frameworks is this?

options.a: A licence fee that rises with every request the agent makes to a model
options.b: A cap on the number of tools that one agent may hold at a time
options.c: A duty to run the model on hardware that the team owns and operates
options.d: Extra layers that obscure the underlying prompts and responses

explanation.d: The post says frameworks "often create extra layers of abstraction that can obscure the underlying prompts and responses, making them harder to debug."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page lists what a framework hides and what it couples: "Your state format, your tool definitions and your tests then follow the framework's releases", and it names no fee.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page lists what a framework gives you, "tool schemas and parsing, retries, tracing hooks", and names no tool cap.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Keeping the model call behind a thin function of your own limits the damage", and the page sets no hardware duty.

quizzes.stem: A product must survive a restart and resume a long task, and the team does not want to operate the sandbox in which the code runs. Which option is the smallest that fits?

options.a: The Messages API, with a loop that the team writes and stores
options.b: Managed Agents, with the session kept on Anthropic's side
options.c: A graph framework, hosted and upgraded by the team itself
options.d: The Claude Code CLI, started by a person every morning

explanation.b: The table gives Managed Agents the task that is "long-running or asynchronous" for those who want "no sandbox to run", with the session stored by Anthropic.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a loop of your own leaves "The loop, the tools, the state" and the sandbox to the team, which is more than the smallest option.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a graph is chosen when you "need its state, resume or typed output, and will pay in coupling", and the team would still host it.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the table row for Managed Agents reads "The task is long-running or asynchronous and you want no sandbox to run", and a person starting a CLI each morning is not a service that resumes.

quizzes.stem: A team must choose between a graph framework and a model-driven loop for a fixed approval chain that regulators audit. Which is better, and why?

options.a: The route written down in code, because it is open to inspection
options.b: The loop, because the model reorders approvals to save time and effort
options.c: The loop, because a model-driven route is easier to reproduce later
options.d: The graph, because it removes the need for any tests of the flow itself

explanation.a: The first page says a graph is for a process that is "known and must be auditable", with the next step decided "You, in advance".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the table gives the next step to "The model, at each turn", and an approval chain must not be reordered.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "The route is whatever the model chooses", and that is harder to reproduce, not easier.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page leaves the checks in place: "Validation proves the shape."

quizzes.stem: A team adopts a framework and later wants to leave it. Which earlier decision would have made leaving cheap?

options.a: Copying the framework's source into the repository of the product
options.b: Using the framework's internal types in every module of the code
options.c: Keeping tools and the model call behind its own thin functions
options.d: Storing the state in the private format that the framework defines

explanation.c: The page says "Keeping the model call behind a thin function of your own limits the damage", and the trap advises "Keep your tools and your model call behind your own functions".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the trap is "Coupling the whole codebase to one framework", and a copy of the source would tie the repository to one.
explanation.b: Ruled out because internal types spread the same coupling: "Your state format, your tool definitions and your tests then follow the framework's releases."
explanation.d: Ruled out because a private state format is the first thing the page lists as following the releases: "Your state format, your tool definitions and your tests".
